speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned inappropriate behavior, changes in eating habits, and weight gain; to understand the root cause, have you noticed any specific symptoms like mood swings, tremors, or excessive thirst recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male. The patient has demonstrated inappropriate behavior, including making unfitting comments and attempts to kiss strangers, over the past 6 months. He shows disinterest in family interactions and has developed a particular craving for chocolate pudding and potato chips, resulting in a 10 kg weight gain. The patient also presents as unkempt.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cushing's Syndrome (likely due to an adrenal tumor or ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma). The classic triad of central obesity, skin changes (implied by unkempt appearance), and neuropsychiatric symptoms (mood lability, inappropriate behavior) alongside specific food cravings and proximal muscle weakness are highly suggestive.

REQUEST TEST: Serum Cortisol (24-hour urinary free cortisol and late-night salivary cortisol). REQUEST TEST: Plasma ACTH level. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal CT scan.
